children: The following are significant news stories, press reports and events on Wednesday. ALL TIMES GMT (Poland: GMT + 2 hours):

Polish interest rates could rise in the near future if the new forecasts from the central bank, due in November, show that high inflation will persist, Iwona Duda, a member of the Monetary Policy Council, told Reuters in an interview.

A Polish court will decide on Wednesday whether to keep in custody a man suspected of planning an attack on the prime minister and defence minister after improvised explosive materials were found in his apartment, prosecutors said.
Norwegian intelligence sees no threat of a Russian invasion, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere told Rzeczpospolita daily.
He added that he does not consider a Russian strike against NATO to be a likely scenario; however, it would be irresponsible to rule it out completely.
Polish retailers have begun removing some Halloween-themed products such as fake knives from shelves following three recent stabbing attacks at schools, company representatives said on Tuesday.

Police have detained two more people in connection with a fire at a Starlink station in Poland last month, private broadcaster RMF FM reported on Tuesday, citing anonymous sources, bringing the total to four.
The Polish Finance Ministry will offer bonds worth 8–12 billion zlotys ($2.05 billion-$3.08 billion) on Wednesday's auction.
****Reuters has not verified stories reported by Polish media and does not vouch for their accuracy.****
